decision: Close NANODA-CACHE-REGRESSION-1 SUCCESS with its current focused/full-suite-validated preventive test and unsubmitted draft. Select SEMANTIC-LET-CONTRACT-1 READY and unstarted: the cache regression and bounded Arena audit now make their shared raw-let typing-versus-reduction question the highest-value feasible cross-project uncertainty, while the remaining implementation, corpus and discovery paths stay independently executable.

categories.assessment: The portfolio now contains two concrete Nanoda test contributions and one bounded Arena outcome packet. A focused primary-source contract clarification is the smallest methodologically distinct next step before more checker-specific discovery or implementation auditing.

The cache test deliberately preserves exported reachability as unresolved, and the Arena let item withholds an unsupported expected outcome. Clarifying raw let typing assumptions can improve both checker-test interpretation and shared corpus language without reopening either completed item.

The new Nanoda patch remains an approval-gated draft; no maintainer response requires immediate follow-through. Negative-cache and nested-name audits remain useful later, while semantic clarification can sharpen any future external explanation before another submission.

The let contract item is explicitly primary-source bounded and can reuse the exact completed control/candidate evidence without treating implementation behavior as authority. HSBM remains the next discovery-oriented method, and import-contract clarification remains a wider semantic alternative.

Every remaining READY item has a finite local entry path. The let question has exact existing examples and an explicit source-only budget, so it can resolve the most immediate shared blocker without a build, checker, proof, mutation or new fixture launch.

candidates.rationale: The completed cache test and Arena audit preserve the same raw malformed-let boundary under different observer scopes. Eight primary-source requests and zero execution launches provide a finite route to qualify the typing judgment, zeta assumptions and any maintainer question.
The bounded six-commit pilot remains a credible discovery path, but known concrete semantic uncertainty should be qualified before seeking more candidates.
The current negative-cache mode/history audit remains locally feasible and may reuse test technique, but it has no fixed behavioral witness and is less cross-project than the let clarification.
The current corpus audit can improve isolation, but its four-case scope and outcome attribution are broader than the exact source-only let question.
Import metadata reconstruction remains a valid independent semantics item, but its grouped fields are wider than the single let obligation now shared by two completed artifacts.
The reserved-namespace regression audit remains independently useful but first needs current attribution and fixture isolation that the let clarification does not require.
